rows.abstract: Rationale: Calling a constitutional convention is believed to be the most democratic mode of proposing amendments, as the will of the people is expressed through their duly elected delegates. rows.abstract: Rationale: For economic reasons, study shows  that a big percent of those who took the board and bar examinations have not attended  a proper review classes. Others deferred taking the licensure exams, and those who failed, hesitantly gambled themselves in getting another chance. This dilemma will cause a tremedous effect and imperil the goals of Philippine education. > Unless remedial measures are adopted to abate the present situation, reviewees will be joining the rooster of frustrated professionals. "Free Review Education Act of 1997" Covers only the first and second times board and bar examinees of the following profession: (1) Accountancy; (2) Architecture; (3) Chemical Engineering; (4) Civil Engineering; (5) Dentistry; (6) Electricaal Engineering; (7) Mechanical Engineering; (8) Medicine; (9) Nursing; (10) Midwifery; (11) Medical Technology; (12) Education; (13) Nautical; (14) Other non-board related licensure examinations; and (15) Law.

rows.abstract: Rationale: "... this bill seeks to lessen the burden in our health care by transforming the Filipinos into a self-reliant nation. This bill seeks to ensure that health care reaches the grass-root level or the rural areas by providing for certain taxincentives to motivate our medical practitioners to work and live in the rural centers." "National Rual Health CAre Act of 1997" Seeks to --- (1) provide all citizens of the Philippines, particularly in the rural or remote areas, to gain access to health services; (2) create the National Rural Health Program, hereinafter referred to as the Program, to serve as the means to help the people avail of health care services; (3) to prioritize and accelerate the provision of health services to all Fillipinos, particularly that segment of the population who cannot avail of such services; and (4) to establish the National Rural Health Care Coordinating Council, hereinafter referred to as the Council, that will administer the Program at all levels.

rows.author: A102
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE WITNESS PROTECTION PROGRAM BY ENTITLING LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICERS TO AVAIL OF ITS BENEFITS IN CASES INVOLVING NATIONAL SECURITY AND HEINOUS CRIMES COMMITTED BY CRIMINAL SYNDICATES, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE SECTION 3, REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6981
rows.abstract: Rationale: Under the Witness Protection, Security and Benefit Law, police and other law enforcers are disqualified from availing of the benefits thereunder (Sec. 3 [d] R.A. 6981). The said disqualificatio n is expressed in absolute terms and does not admit of exceptions. This restriction is not promotive of full protection to law officers and is prejudicial to national interest. Needless to state, the disqualificatio n likewise tends to discriminate law enforcers. > States that ANY ENFORCEMENTOFFICER may be entitled to the Witness Protection Program IF THE OFFENSE IN WHICH HIS TESTIMONY WILL BE USED INVOLVES NATIONAL SECURITY OR IS COMMITTED BY AN ORGANIZED CRIMINAL SYNDICATE WHERE THE IMPOSABLE PENALTY IS DEATH.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 1997-12-08

rows.abstract: Rationale: The rationale behind this proposal is the fact and truth that actual residents in the barangays, municipalities or provinces where business or non-business establishments are lcoated have enchoate rights and preferences for labor and employment opportunities over others who are not actual residents. They are the very first persons to be directly affected by its establishment and operation, be it for the better or worse. Any employment opportunities and other fruits for the actual residents and government thereat should exclusively belong to them.  This is only fair and just. > "The Residents' Employment and Security Act" > Provides for the following --- "SECTION 2. Coverage and Application. - It shall be unlawful for any person,, coporation or association to hire or employ directly or indirectly any employee or worker who is not an actual resident in barangay, municipality or province where the said employer or employers had established or may establish his company, corpora

rows.author: B041
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING PENALTY FOR ANY EMPLOYER WHO TERMINATES EMPLOYMENT WITHOUT JUST CAUSE WHILE UNDER PROBATION TO AVOID REGULARIZATION AND SECURITY OF TENURE
rows.abstract: Rationale: All over nationwide, more specifically in food and chain establishments and other fields of industries, there is rampant violations of these statutory and constitutional guarantees to labor.  These are violated grossly and wantonly at will, left and right, and with impunity. Our small and poor workers are a very pitiful sight because the practice which is openly public is that once these young workers are in the fifth (5th) month, they are cruelly terminated WITHOUT JUST CAUSE OR CAUSES. Why? Are these young workers not entitled at all to regularization and security of tenure? Let us now put a stop to this mockery to our Labor Code and the Constitution. > "The Employees' Regularization Law" Provides for the following --- "SECTIOON 3. Prohibited Acts. - It shall be unlawful for any employer to terminate any employee or worker on or before the expiration of a period of six (6) months from date of employment without just, valid and legal cause in order to prevent or avoid regu

rows.abstract: Rationale: The Supreme Court, in people vs. Reyes (GR. From the preceding disquisition, the obvious rsposte is that this is a matter which should be properly addressed to by the legislature. It is not for this Court, by judicial legislation, to amend the pertinent provisions of the Revised Penal Code. x x x On this score, we can take judicial notice that multimillion or large-scale estafa cases and inveterate or professional swindlers have iinflicted untold damages and misery not only on one or two but on countless victims in this country." > Seeks, therefore, to REPEAL PD No. 818, Amending Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code by Increasing the Penalties for Estafa Committed by Means o

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 226, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS INVESTMENTS CODE OF 1987 AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES(RE: CUSTOMS DUTIES AND VAT ON CA PITAL EQUIPMENT)
rows.abstract: Rationale: Republic Act No. 7918, amending Article 39 of Executive Order No. 226, otherwise known as the Omnibus Investments Code of 1987, provides that importations of capital equipment, machinery and spare parts of enterprises registered with theBoard of Investments after 31 December 1994 are subject to 3% customs duties and 10% value added tax.  However, this is set to expire on 31 December 1997. > The present situation wherein the Philippine economy is being affected by the current capital/financi al turmoil in Asia has brought up the cost of operations of industries in the country. Withi this situation and the expiration of the capital equipment incentive, the next few years would see a loss in momentum in the gains made by the counttry in attracting the very much needed investments into Philippine industries. > Seeks to EXTEND the current state of capital equipment incentives as embodied in RA No. 7918 up to December 31, 1999.
